Looking at this question about the E. coli Long-Term Evolution Experiment (LTEE) and transcription in non-genic regions at 50,000 generations:

This question refers to genomic studies of the LTEE lines that examined transcriptional activity in intergenic/non-genic regions. In E. coli genomics, it is well established that at relaxed detection thresholds, a very high proportion of non-genic regions show some level of transcriptional activity (cryptic transcription, promoter-like activity, transcriptional noise, etc.).

At relaxed thresholds for transcription detection in the LTEE E. coli lines at 50,000 generations, approximately 95% of non-genic genomic region windows displayed some transcription.
